research_mode: official ONS, OSR and Police.uk sources only; current crime-statistics production and designation, 2025-2027 crime-data-integrity inspection design, IT and QA oversight, NDQIS and PND quality controls, and stop-search precision and missing-state contracts; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Current crime statistics user guide version
verified_claims: the current user guide is the March 2026 edition
the page was revised on 5 June 2026
edition and revision date must be pinned
limitations: page revision can change methodology text
not parcel-level evidence

sources.name: Police recorded crime statistical designation
verified_claims: most police recorded crime statistics are official statistics rather than accredited official statistics
accreditation was removed in 2014
unlawful-death statistics based on the Homicide Index were restored separately
limitations: designation varies by product
accreditation status is not a parcel-confidence score

sources.name: Police recorded crime collection chain
verified_claims: data originate from 43 territorial forces plus British Transport Police
returns are derived from local force record-management systems
notifiable-offence data are supplied monthly
limitations: local systems differ
monthly supply does not prove uniform recording quality

sources.name: Police recorded crime production cadence
verified_claims: Home Office Crime Analysis Unit quality assures the force data
final data are sent to ONS at quarter end
ONS publishes aggregate statistics quarterly and annually
limitations: quarterly publication lags operational recording
aggregate publication cannot reproduce record-level QA

sources.name: Police recorded crime geography and timeliness
verified_claims: statistics are published on a rolling 12-month basis
national, Police Force Area and Community Safety Partnership levels are available
reports are typically published within four months of the period
limitations: PFA and CSP are not LSOA or parcel geographies
publication timeliness is not event timeliness

sources.name: National Crime Recording Standard decision rule
verified_claims: NCRS was introduced across England and Wales in April 2002
it uses a victim-oriented approach
an allegation meeting the legal test is recorded unless credible contrary evidence is immediately available
limitations: recording rules create time-series breaks
the rule does not prove every local decision was correct

sources.name: Administrative-data quality factors
verified_claims: police recorded crime is administrative data
quality is affected by recording rules and systems
human error and operational resource decisions can affect figures
limitations: observed changes may mix crime and process effects
factors vary across forces

sources.name: Police-activity sensitivity
verified_claims: proactive policing can increase recorded drug or weapon offences
the increase may occur without a matching change in underlying crime
commentary and caveats are required for trends
limitations: activity effects differ by offence
not suitable as a direct safety score

sources.name: Recording-practice trend limitation
verified_claims: changes in recording practices affect violent and sexual offence trends
improved NCRS compliance increased recorded counts
the scale and force variation cannot be fully quantified
limitations: recorded figures may be better indicators of police activity than underlying trends
historical comparisons require caveats

sources.name: 2025 national crime-recording accuracy summary
verified_claims: the 2025 summary reports 94.8 percent for all crime excluding fraud
93.6 percent for violent crime
95.9 percent for sexual offences
limitations: national estimates are not force or parcel values
inspection sampling uncertainty remains relevant
